title: Causal inference in conjoint analysis: Understanding multidimensional choices via stated preference experiments
rationale: The article reports candidate and immigration conjoint experiments with repeated pairs of profiles and independently varying attributes (physical pages 4–5). These are genuine survey experiments but require a conjoint structure outside the simple fixed-arm parser.

title: Helping victims of intimate partner violence: The influence of group norms among lay people and the police
rationale: Both studies manipulate written information about group norms in paper-and-pencil questionnaires: helping versus not helping versus control among students, and arrest versus no arrest versus control among police. Outcomes are reported intentions. The three fixed conditions appear compatible in principle; original questionnaire files have not been parsed.

title: Three experimental approaches to measure the social context dependence of prejudice communication and discriminatory behavior
rationale: The article combines a simple question-order experiment, a single-vignette factorial survey, and a repeated discrete-choice experiment involving three alternatives with multiple attributes. The latter requires a choice-set parser; simpler component studies may be usable separately.

title: In-group bias in children's intention to help can be overpowered by inducing empathy
rationale: Two written helping stories share a fixed between-subjects manipulation of empathy induction, friend status, and need, followed by rated helping intentions. There are no multi-attribute choice sets; the two fixed story outcomes appear compatible in principle, subject to inspection of original questionnaire files.

title: She’s Not a Person.. She’s Just a Woman! Infra-Humanization and Intimate Partner Violence
rationale: A paper-and-pencil survey presents a written intimate-partner-violence vignette and varies whether the victim admits or denies infidelity. Participants then report perceptions and willingness to help. This two-condition design appears compatible in principle; the original instrument has not been parsed.

title: Inoculation in competitive framing examining message effects on policy preferences
rationale: The article randomizes written tax-framing and inoculation messages across eight fixed conditions over two survey waves. It is a survey experiment, but combining treatment sequences, repeat outcomes, and linked-wave records needs original instrument and data inspection before parser compatibility can be established.

title: First Arrival and Collective Land Ownership: How Children Reason About Who Owns the Land
rationale: Four experiments randomize fixed picture-story or text variants and collect ownership, liking, or pride judgments on paper questionnaires. This is eligible survey-experimental content, but the cartoon stimuli and paper instrument require inspection before parser compatibility can be confirmed.

title: When is Changing Policy Positions Costly for Politicians? Experimental Evidence
rationale: Two between-respondent experiments vary a single written candidate biography and collect fixed evaluation items. The appendices provide vignette variants and response wording; randomized policy attributes do not by themselves make this a repeated paired-profile conjoint. The described structure appears compatible, subject to inspection of the original survey and data files.

title: Improving Survey Response Rates in Online Panels: Effects of Low-Cost Incentives and Cost-Free Text Appeal Interventions
rationale: The experiment randomizes invitation-email incentives or appeals and tests whether panelists take a survey. Its reported endpoint is participation rather than a judgment, belief, intention, preference, or comparable response to experimental content within a survey; the fixed invitation experiment therefore does not fit the target data/parser workflow. This flag does not change article counts.

title: The conditional nature of the local warming effect
rationale: A fixed two-arm survey randomizes a brief written corrective prompt before climate-belief, worry, and attribution items; a week-later follow-up repeats outcomes without another treatment. The first-wave structure is compatible in principle; the follow-up outcomes must be mapped separately when inspecting original files.

title: A Bottom-Up Theory of Public Opinion about Foreign Policy
rationale: The article reports five eligible content experiments measuring support for foreign policies. Experiments 1–2 use a crossover with linked treatment reversals, while social cues include bar graphs; experiment 3 has a simpler twelve-cell factorial. Survey files, visual materials, and study/wave mapping require inspection before article-level parser compatibility is established.

title: The Number of Choice Tasks and Survey Satisficing in Conjoint Experiments
rationale: The paper reports six new survey experiments that randomize candidate attributes and elicit choices between profiles. Thirty paired-profile tasks per respondent constitute a conjoint design that the current parser cannot handle. Broad survey-experiment eligibility and US geography remain separate from this compatibility flag; no count exclusion is applied.

title: Communicating with providers about racial healthcare disparities: The role of providers’ prior beliefs on their receptivity to different narrative frames
rationale: A fixed three-arm narrative experiment measures immediate identification and behavioral intentions, plus a four-week self-report follow-up. Its immediate survey component appears compatible; combining follow-up outcomes would require participant linkage. No article exclusion is applied.

title: Information and Issue Constraints on Party Cues
rationale: A fixed twelve-condition assignment varies party cues and substantive information across three news stories, each followed by policy ratings. This appears compatible with a conventional survey-treatment structure; actual source files have not been tested.

title: On the Meaning of Survey Reports of Roll-Call “Votes”
rationale: Three original experiments assign fixed information conditions before repeated judgments about legislation or court cases. Repeated question batteries do not themselves imply conjoint profiles; no complex adaptive task is apparent.

title: Demand effects in survey experiments: An empirical assessment
rationale: The article includes simple written framing, welfare and resume experiments as well as a paired-news conjoint task, all crossed with demand-effect manipulations. Some study components fit the target format, but the combined article-level dataset needs study selection before parser compatibility can be established.

title: Ethical climate(s), organizational identification, and employees' behavior
rationale: Two experiments vary fixed descriptions of an organization’s ethical climate before identification, commitment and intention questions. The second adds a fixed alternative-job scenario; no conjoint or adaptive interaction is apparent.
